title: Machine learning screens hardness and oxidation resistance in refractory alloys
summary: XGBoost hardness and random forest oxidation models (held-out R2 0.79 and 0.76) screened 109,571 quinary compositions, and six alloys were fabricated for contrasting hardness-oxidation trade-offs, with measured hardness up to 780 +/- 8 HV and a lowest specific mass gain of 2.75 +/- 0.04 mg/cm2 after 1000 C for 20 h. A refined gradient boosting oxidation model (held-out R2 0.94) cut mean absolute oxidation index error from 0.46 to 0.21 on three further alloys, and the refined candidate had 661 +/- 11 HV and a mass gain of 6.20 +/- 0.01 mg/cm2.
ai_technology: XGBoost, random forest and gradient boosting models with SHAP analysis
organization: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique; National Tsing Hua University; Institut de Chimie de la Matière Condensée de Bordeaux

evidence.tested: Experimental synthesis and measurement of nine alloys chosen by model predictions.
evidence.unknown: Few experimental candidates; initial oxidation predictions had large errors; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning models screened composition space and prioritized alloys for synthesis.
